title: Pool_Exhaustion crisis can never resolve when pool_max_packets == 1 (clamp guard excludes cap 1)
evidence:
+			pool_margin := CRISIS_RESOLVE_MARGIN
+			if cat.balance.pool_max_packets > 1 && u32(cat.balance.pool_max_packets) <= pool_margin {
+				pool_margin = u32(cat.balance.pool_max_packets) - 1
+			}
+			cleared = len(state.flow.packets) + int(pool_margin) < int(cat.balance.pool_max_packets) &&
+				!drop_of_reason_this_tick(state, .Pool_Exhaustion)
---
+  - **W-2 — the pool-cap margin clamp**: a catalog pool cap of 1-2 (legal values) could never resolve
+    a Pool_Exhaustion crisis (resolve needs len + 2 < cap; the E9 path has the N5 clamp, the pool none).
+    The pool margin now clamps to cap-1 (resolve + the trigger's anti-flap); the shipped 512 is
+    unaffected (authoring-time caps covered).
detail: At cap 1 the `> 1` guard skips the clamp, so resolve requires `len + 2 < 1` — unsatisfiable. A cap-1 pool crisis fires (trigger margin clamps to 0) and persists forever, contradicting W-2's claim that caps 1-2 are covered.
recommended_fix: Clamp with `pool_max_packets >= 1` (margin = cap-1, i.e. 0 at cap 1), mirroring the E9 resolve clamp's `bound > 0` guard.

title: Dead email_e22 accumulation in pool-crisis test — computed, never asserted, and self-admittedly meaningless
detail: `email_e22` is computed and never read; the adjacent comment admits the scratch holds only the last tick's sites, so the loop proves nothing and misleads. Dead test code.
recommended_fix: Delete the loop and the variable; keep only the SLA-accumulator assertion.

title: bundle_class_queue takes an unused cat parameter
detail: The proc body never references `cat`, though every sibling helper (bundle_lane_at, crisis_bundle_saturated) uses it. The signature advertises catalog-dependent behavior it does not have.

title: Renumber test comment says the demolish applies at tick 1301 but apply_tick is 1300
detail: crisis_record_run applies commands when cmd.apply_tick == tick, so the island demolish applies at tick 1300. The comment's 1301 and the renumber-tick narrative are off by one.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment to tick 1300 or set apply_tick = 1301 so comment and code agree.

title: Pool test comment claims the 1500 fix 'applies at 1501's step' — contradicted by the sibling test's tick-1500 pins
detail: test_crisis_resolve_and_retrigger draws wides via sla_draw(..., 1500) and pins the re-trigger at tick 1500 — commands apply at apply_tick, not +1. The pool test's '(applies at 1501's step)' claim is false.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to 'applies at tick 1500's step'.

title: Lint gate 6 scanner can miss non-ASCII in render string literals (comment-split truncation, no escape handling)
evidence:
+	code = line.split(\"//\")[0]
---
+	for ch in code:
+		if ch == q:
+			in_str = not in_str
detail: `line.split(\"//\")[0]` truncates any literal containing '//' before scanning, so non-ASCII bytes after it escape detection; the quote toggling ignores escaped quotes, desyncing the state machine. The mojibake gate is bypassable.
recommended_fix: Scan the full line before stripping comments and handle escaped quotes in the string-state machine.

title: Spec's frozen Events bullet promises 'pre-4.2 streams byte-identical' while the code extends the drop payload and admits streams are NOT byte-identical
evidence:
+- **Events (ODN-14, append-only):** `EVENT_TAG_CRISIS_TRIGGERED :: u8(8)` / `EVENT_TAG_CRISIS_RESOLVED :: u8(9)`; payload `{archetype, cause(kind), class, target(bundle), pipe}` via new Event fields `archetype: u8`, `cause: u8`, `pipe: u32` — tag-conditional serialization, pre-4.2 streams byte-identical.
---
+// Packet_Dropped shed-bundle byte (the DOCUMENTED payload extension — pre-4.2
+// drop payloads were class+reason only, so pre-4.2 event streams are NOT
+// byte-identical; the 4.2 re-bless covers the fold) and the tags 8/9 crisis
+// payloads (genuinely append-only).
detail: The in-review spec body asserts pre-4.2 byte-identity; the code adds a +4-byte drop payload and says the opposite. The contradiction is acknowledged only in the change log (W3-carry), not in the bullet that still reads as contract.
recommended_fix: Annotate the frozen Events bullet as superseded in the bullet itself, not only in the change log.

title: test_crisis_replay_identity never replays from an action log — it re-runs the same seeded sim twice in memory
evidence:
+	// the SAME run twice: byte-identical hash sequences (E10 — the crisis
+	// state + events ride the T1 hash, so a divergent engine would diverge
+	// here).
+	h1 := run(cat)
+	defer delete(h1)
+	h2 := run(cat)
---
+- Given any run, when it replays from the action log, then identical crisis state + event stream (E10); post-terminal ticks stay frozen (E17).
detail: The spec's acceptance requires replay-from-action-log identity; this chunk's only replay evidence exercises in-memory determinism from the seed. The derived cooldown bookkeeping recomputation under a real serialized-log re-sim is not covered here.
recommended_fix: Add a record_run-style serialized-log re-sim, or cite the harness replay gate as the acceptance evidence.
